title: Annotation-only data pruning for instance segmentation
method: Training-free, model-independent image-level pruning for instance segmentation from mask annotations only. Per instance: boundary complexity P/A of the largest contour, made scale-invariant (P / 2√(πA)) and class-balanced (divided by the sum of scores over all instances of that class); the image score sums its instances' scores; keep the top-K highest-scoring (hardest) images. No model, training or tunable hyperparameters beyond the budget. Also a generic recipe to adapt classification-oriented, model-based pruning criteria to instance segmentation by aggregating per-pixel scores to an image score.

compute.hardware: A few GPUs: a single 24 GB consumer GPU up to two 80 GB data-center GPUs

claims.text: This is the first training-free, model-independent dataset pruning framework for instance segmentation

A boundary-complexity score computed from mask annotations alone identifies informative training images; its scale-invariant and class-balanced refinements handle instance-area variation and class imbalance
At the same data budget, subsets selected this way train better instance-segmentation models than subsets chosen by existing (adapted) model-based pruning criteria
Because selection does not depend on a model, the subsets carry over across CNN- and Transformer-based segmentation architectures
Selection costs far less than with model-based criteria, which must train a model first
A recipe for adapting classification-oriented pruning criteria to instance segmentation, to serve as reference methods for this new setting

questions.hypothesis: Your method beats random and the adapted baselines at matched budget
questions.predictionIfFalse: It wins only at some budgets (hard-sample selection is known to degrade at small budgets)

questions.hypothesis: Your gain survives these controls and shows up in Boundary AP
questions.predictionIfFalse: Instance count alone matches your method

questions.text: Ablations on the six design choices (raw score, scale-invariant normalization, class-balanced normalization, largest contour only, image aggregation, selection direction), plus sensitivity to implementation details
Cross-architecture transfer: do subsets transfer across Mask R-CNN, Mask2Former R50 and Mask2Former Swin-T, and do model-based baselines show a matched-vs-mismatched transfer gap?
questions.hypothesis: The baselines show a transfer gap, while yours is architecture-agnostic by construction (retention numbers must show it is good for every architecture)

questions.text: Selection cost: wall-clock time and GPU-hours of each method's whole pipeline on the same hardware, total cost to a trained model vs full-data training, and break-even points
Adaptation recipe: which choices in the per-pixel to image aggregation step matter, for several criteria?
questions.hypothesis: The adapted criteria beat random somewhere
questions.predictionIfFalse: Adapted criteria never beat random: the references are weak and the claim of a useful recipe fails

questions.text: Robustness and limits: simple smooth masks, very high pruning, crowd/ambiguous/erroneous annotations
questions.hypothesis: Less signal on a dataset with simple, smooth masks; the hardest-first strategy degrades at very high pruning (90%)
